articles.title: Witness History - The start of the World Trade Organization - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: In 1994, the agreement that created the World Trade Organization was signed in Morrocco
articles.body:
World Service , · 23 Nov 2026 , · 10 mins

In 1994, government trade ministers and ambassadors from around the world gathered in Marrakesh, Morrocco to sign the agreement that created the World Trade Organization (WTO), the body that helps countries trade with each other by agreeing common rules and settling trade disputes. Twenty-three thousand pages, one hundred and twenty delegates and last-minute negotiations. The build up to the signing the Marrakesh agreement was challenging. Said El Hachimi was a young Moroccan trade official helping organise the historic summit. He tells Gill Kearsley about the huge logistical challenges, the royal banquet he almost missed, and witnessing a new era in global trade begin. Witness History is a short BBC World Service podcast about history that takes you inside big moments from the past through first-hand testimony and archive. Each weekday, in around nine minutes, we revisit one moment that helped shape the world and hear it through the voice of someone who was there. Scientists, artists, campaigners, soldiers, leaders and everyday people tell their true stories. When you subscribe to Witness History, you’ll be taken inside turning points in world affairs from West Africa’s fight back against Boko Haram in 2015 to the behind-closed-doors talks that led to the US-Cuba “thaw” and the surprise announcement of restored relations. You’ll discover what it was like to experience disasters and how people recovered from them, including the Tabasco floods in Mexico, Portugal's worst train disaster, and the huge clean-up after the Chernobyl nuclear disaster. You’ll explore culture and ideas too: Sweden’s Expedition Robinson, often credited as the first modern reality TV game show; the friendship between The Beatles’ George Harrison and Indian sitarist Ravi Shankar; and the night a tiger attack brought Las Vegas superstars Siegfried and Roy’s show to a sudden end. And if you’re curious about inventions, we’ll tell you how air fryers, BlackBerry, YouTube, Alexa, GPS, superglue, the shopping cart (shopping trolley) and bubble tea were created. If you’re new to Witness History, the appeal is simple: real voices, one strong true story, and a fresh way to understand today through events from history – all in the time it takes to enjoy a cup of tea or a walk around the block. Join millions of BBC World Service podcast listeners around the globe and enjoy the insight, context and detail Witness History will bring you. (Photo: The signing of the Marrakesh agreement. Credit: Abdelhak Senna/AFP via Getty Images)

articles.body:

Student demonstrators demanding better conditions have been joined by yellow vest activists and others, angry about the rising cost of living.

articles.title: Money Box - New Bank Services Law and Investment Scams - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: The money stolen by criminals through fake investments doubles in just two years.
articles.body: The government has set out a new law to force banks to make sure customers have access to face to face banking. The amendment to a Bill already going through Parliament came this week as a report was published warning that urgent action was needed to prevent "further harm" to people who need to go into a bank in person. This major review into access to banking was commissioned by the Treasury because of the continuing loss of branches from all the major banks. Paul Lewis interviews Richard Lloyd, who wrote this report. New figures seen exclusively by Money Box show the amount of money taken in investment scams has doubled in just two years. In the first six months of this year UK Finance figures show more than one hundred million pounds was stolen from thousands of people, with experts saying the use of artificial intelligence is one of the reasons behind the rise. Heating your home will cost more in January - but seven different payments may help with those bills. What are they and who's eligible? And, as we approach Black Friday, how to protect your money from fake offers and bargains. articles.summary: President Zelensky said a Russia warship was sunk, with a Russian cargo ship also hit.
articles.body:
Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky has shared footage on social media which he says shows strikes on Russian vessels off the coast of Libya on Sunday.

A Russian warship was sunk by Ukrainian drones and the attack also targeted a second vessel, a cargo ship which was being used to transport weapons, Zelensky said.

Footage verified by the BBC shows a ship ablaze at Benghazi's port.

The local health ministry said it had received injured people from a commercial ship that was targeted off the coast. It is not clear whether this is the same vessel as the one Ukraine has claimed responsibility for.

Following the strikes, the Kremlin warned of an "escalation of tensions in the region", but declined to comment directly on the attacks in Libya.

articles.title: Barco no Pará: famílias reagem  à identificação de mortos em deriva | G1
articles.standfirst: Barco foi encontrado à deriva no litoral paraense em abril de 2024, com nove corpos; investigação percorreu mais de 1,5 mil km na África para localizar familiares e coletar material genético de possíveis vítimas.
articles.summary: Após percorrer 1,5 mil km na África, investigação identifica seis migrantes que morreram em barco à deriva encontrado no Pará com nove corpos em abril de 2024.
articles.body:
"Agora à noite, quando eu me deitar, vou dormir melhor, porque sei que ele morreu."

A frase é de Kouna Cissé, um pai que passou dois anos sem notícias do filho, Sidy, desaparecido durante uma travessia pelo oceano Atlântico. O jovem estava entre os passageiros de uma embarcação encontrada à deriva no litoral do Pará , em abril de 2024, com nove corpos.

A confirmação da morte, embora dolorosa, trouxe ao pai uma resposta que ele esperava havia anos. O caso faz parte de uma investigação internacional que mobilizou autoridades brasileiras, peritos e uma jornalista para descobrir a origem do barco, identificar as vítimas e localizar suas famílias na África.

A embarcação percorreu cerca de 4 mil quilômetros à deriva durante aproximadamente 80 dias. Ela havia saído de Nouadhibou, cidade portuária da Mauritânia, em 23 de janeiro de 2024, com migrantes que pretendiam chegar às Ilhas Canárias, arquipélago espanhol na costa africana.

Durante a viagem, o barco ficou sem motor e sem leme e acabou sendo levado pelas correntes marítimas e pelos ventos do Atlântico até a costa brasileira.

Quando foi encontrado por pescadores paraenses, em 13 de abril daquele ano, havia oito corpos dentro da embarcação e um nono nas proximidades.

Famílias de migrantes reagem ao descobrir que parentes estavam em embarcação encontrada no Pará — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Entre os documentos encontrados no barco estava o de Suleiman Gassama, nascido em 1983, na Mauritânia. A identificação do documento permitiu que a jornalista Renata Brito, da agência Associated Press (AP), entrasse em contato com a mulher dele, Cadiatu.

Suleiman havia deixado a Mauritânia em janeiro de 2024. Na época, o filho mais novo tinha apenas um ano de idade.

Sem notícias do marido, Cadiatu precisou lidar com a ausência e com as dificuldades práticas de comprovar o desaparecimento. Para matricular os filhos na escola, por exemplo, era necessário apresentar o documento de identidade do pai. Caso informasse que ele havia morrido, a família precisaria apresentar uma certidão de óbito.

A falta de respostas também afetava as crianças.

“Minha filha me dizia: ‘Mamãe, eu não quero mais comer, guarde o dinheiro do pão para ir procurar o papai.’”

A investigação só conseguiu avançar depois que documentos, anotações e outros objetos encontrados na embarcação foram analisados. Ao todo, havia 28 celulares no barco.

Investigação percorreu mais de 1,5 mil km na África

Mais de dois anos depois da descoberta da embarcação, uma equipe brasileira foi à Mauritânia para localizar familiares, recolher amostras de DNA e tentar identificar os nove corpos.

Em junho, o perito Alexandre Deitos, formado em odontologia, percorreu mais de 1,5 mil quilômetros pelo país, acompanhado pela jornalista Renata Brito e pelos fotógrafos Felipe Dana e Bram Jensen.

A missão também chegou a famílias no Mali. Em um papel encontrado dentro do barco, uma palavra escrita à mão chamou a atenção dos investigadores: "Mamã", que significa mãe em francês. Abaixo dela, havia um número de telefone.

O contato levou até Bambi Cissé, mãe de Moussa Samba Kamarat, um militar que estava desaparecido. Ela compareceu com os dois netos para fornecer material genético.

Em outro caso, os investigadores encontraram pistas que poderiam ajudar a identificar um dos passageiros por meio de registros médicos. O homem havia passado por uma cirurgia no tornozelo, e um dos corpos encontrados no Brasil tinha pinos na mesma região.

A comparação com registros hospitalares anteriores poderia ajudar na identificação, mesmo sem a necessidade de um exame de DNA.

Durante a missão, a equipe conseguiu reunir 85 amostras de material genético de pessoas ligadas a 29 famílias.

Em 9 de outubro, um comitê de identificação formalizou a identidade de seis das nove vítimas encontradas na embarcação.

Entre os identificados estava Suleiman Gassama. A confirmação foi comunicada à família, que finalmente recebeu uma resposta sobre o desaparecimento.

"Meu guerreiro fez tudo o que podia. Foi até o fim."

O trabalho também ajudou a ampliar a lista de possíveis passageiros. A equipe chegou à Mauritânia com alguns nomes e voltou com 42. A relação, porém, ainda estava incompleta, e os investigadores não conseguiram estabelecer o número exato de pessoas que estavam no barco.

Uma das hipóteses para a diferença entre o número de passageiros e os nove corpos encontrados é que, durante os meses à deriva, pessoas que morreram tenham sido lançadas ao mar.

Rota migratória registrou mais de mil mortes em 2024

Os passageiros tentavam percorrer a chamada Rota Atlântica da África Ocidental, utilizada por migrantes que saem de países do noroeste africano em direção às Ilhas Canárias, na Espanha.

A travessia é marcada por embarcações precárias e longos percursos pelo oceano. Em busca de trabalho e melhores condições de vida, muitas pessoas se arriscam na viagem.

Em 2024, ano em que o barco deixou a Mauritânia, a Organização Internacional para as Migrações (OIM), ligada à Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU), registrou 62 naufrágios nessa rota. Ao todo, 1.070 pessoas morreram ou desapareceram.

A própria organização alerta que o número pode ser maior, já que muitos naufrágios não chegam a ser registrados.

Para as famílias, a identificação dos corpos representa a possibilidade de finalmente saber o que aconteceu com seus parentes e, em alguns casos, buscar o retorno dos restos mortais ao país de origem.

"É direito da família receber o seu corpo e é direito da pessoa ter um tratamento digno, ter um enterro digno", afirmou o perito Alexandre Deitos.

Mais de mil dias depois da partida da embarcação, a investigação conseguiu levar respostas a algumas das famílias. Para outras, a espera continua.

articles.title: Brinquedo pega fogo em shopping de Marabá  | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso ocorreu no domingo, 22. Testemunhas relatam que carrinho elétrico passou por conserto improvisado na bateria antes de começar a soltar fumaça e andar sozinho.
articles.summary: Após carrinho elétrico pegar fogo e andar sozinho em shopping de Marabá, a administração suspendeu a atração e solicitou laudos técnicos de segurança.
articles.body:
Brinquedo pega fogo dentro de shopping em Marabá, no Pará — Foto: TV Liberal

Um brinquedo elétrico pegou fogo e causou assustou frequentadores de um shopping em Marabá , no sudeste do Pará, na tarde deste domingo (22). Apesar do susto, ninguém ficou ferido.

De acordo com testemunhas, o carrinho elétrico estava sendo utilizado por crianças momentos antes do ocorrido. Frequentadores afirmaram que a bateria de um dos brinquedos caiu e, em seguida, os funcionários realizaram um conserto improvisado para recolocar o veículo em funcionamento.

Pouco tempo após o reparo, o brinquedo voltou a ser usado, mas começou a soltar fumaça. A criança que estava a bordo desceu do veículo imediatamente.

Enquanto o carrinho era empurrado de volta para a área da empresa responsável, ele pegou fogo e começou a se movimentar sozinho, sem controle, em direção a uma loja de quadros e decoração.

Um empresário que passava pelo local ainda chegou a puxar o brinquedo em chamas e evitar que ele atingisse o estabelecimento. A brigada de incêndio do shopping e bombeiros civis foram acionados e conseguiram conter o fogo utilizando os equipamentos de segurança do próprio empreendimento.

Em nota, a administração do shopping disse que o caso foi controlado imediatamente pela equipe de segurança e que o sistema de emergência foi acionado para mobilizar a brigada.

Como medida preventiva, a direção do shopping determinou a suspensão imediata das atividades da atração e a retirada de todos os brinquedos e carrinhos de circulação.

Os equipamentos permanecerão interditados até que as inspeções técnicas sejam concluídas e os laudos de segurança apresentados.

O shopping também reforçou que a segurança de clientes, lojistas e colaboradores é prioridade e que a retomada do serviço está condicionada à comprovação de que todos os itens atendem às exigências técnicas de segurança.

articles.title: Correnteza toma ruas de Ubatuba após chuva e Defesa Civil faz alerta | G1
articles.standfirst: Cidade registrou até 146 milímetros de chuva em 24 horas. Temporal provocou alagamentos, deslizamento de terra e queda de árvores na Rio-Santos.
articles.summary: Cidade registrou até 146 milímetros de chuva em 24 horas. Temporal provocou alagamentos, deslizamento de terra e queda de árvores na Rio-Santos.
articles.body:
A forte chuva que atingiu Ubatuba , no Litoral Norte de São Paulo, na noite de domingo (22), provocou alagamentos e transformou ruas em rios em diferentes pontos da cidade. Imagens registradas por moradores mostram a força da correnteza passando pelas vias, principalmente na região do Taquaral.

Um corpo foi encontrado em um rio da cidade após a enchente. A Polícia investiga a possibilidade de uma motocicleta ter caído no rio com a vítima. A Prefeitura informou que apura se a pessoa foi vítima da enchente, mas ainda não há confirmação de relação entre a morte e as chuvas. A identidade não foi divulgada - saiba mais clicando aqui.

A chuva começou por volta das 22h30 e atingiu toda a cidade. Os bairros Taquaral, Vila Resende e Centro registraram os maiores impactos. Na Comunidade do Angelim, no Taquaral, um vídeo feito por uma moradora mostra a água avançando com força pela rua, carregando volume e velocidade semelhantes aos de um rio.

Ubatuba registrou um dos maiores volumes de chuva do país nas últimas 24 horas, conforme balanço das 7h. Segundo a Defesa Civil estadual, foram 145 milímetros no período, o maior acumulado registrado no Brasil neste domingo (22).

Dados das seis estações do Centro Nacional de Monitoramento e Alertas de Desastres Naturais (Cemaden) instaladas na cidade apontam volumes ainda maiores em alguns pontos.

Além dos alagamentos, um deslizamento de terra foi registrado na região da Praia da Fortaleza. Também houve queda de árvores na Rodovia Rio-Santos, no trecho norte, no sentido Rio de Janeiro.

A Defesa Civil estadual informou que segue monitorando os impactos das fortes chuvas no estado, por meio do Centro de Gerenciamento de Emergências. O órgão mantém alerta para a possibilidade de novas precipitações e informou que o cenário ainda é de chuva persistente, com risco de novos temporais.

articles.title: Quais são os próximos feriados de 2026? Veja o único que resta | G1
articles.standfirst: O Natal, em 25 de dezembro, será o último feriado nacional do ano; vésperas de Natal e de Ano-Novo serão pontos facultativos.
articles.summary: O Natal, em 25 de dezembro, será o último feriado nacional do ano; vésperas de Natal e de Ano-Novo serão pontos facultativos.
articles.body:
Decoração Natal Luz em Gramado — Foto: Cleiton Thiele/ SerraPress

Após o feriadão da Consciência Negra, celebrado na sexta-feira (20), muitos trabalhadores já estão de olho no próximo período de descanso. A data permitiu emendar três dias de folga para quem não precisou trabalhar no fim de semana.

O ano está chegando ao fim, e o próximo feriado nacional será o Natal, em 25 de dezembro , daqui a cerca de um mês. Antes disso, as vésperas de Natal (24) e de Ano-Novo (31) serão pontos facultativos, conforme o calendário oficial. (veja o calendário abaixo)

Nem todos os trabalhadores têm direito à folga nos feriados. A legislação permite o funcionamento de atividades consideradas essenciais e de outras categorias autorizadas a trabalhar nessas datas.

⚠️ Nesses casos, quem trabalha no feriado pode ter direito a remuneração em dobro ou a uma folga compensatória , conforme a legislação aplicável e as regras previstas em acordos ou convenções coletivas.

Ao todo, 2026 terá 10 feriados nacionais, dos quais nove cairão em dias úteis . Algumas datas permitem planejar períodos prolongados de descanso, especialmente para quem já folga aos fins de semana.

Depois do Dia da Consciência Negra, em 20 de novembro, restará apenas o Natal, celebrado em 25 de dezembro, uma sexta-feira . A data forma três dias seguidos de descanso para quem não trabalha aos fins de semana.

Já as vésperas de Natal (24) e de Ano-Novo (31) serão pontos facultativos para os órgãos e entidades abrangidos pelo calendário oficial do governo federal . No setor privado, a concessão de folga nessas datas não é automática.

articles.standfirst: Policiais de imigração vestiam jaquetas sem identificação. Os detidos são mexicanos e, segundo a defesa, vivem nos EUA desde 2015 e não têm antecedentes criminais.
articles.summary: Policiais de imigração vestiam jaquetas sem identificação. Os detidos são mexicanos e, segundo a defesa, vivem nos EUA desde 2015 e não têm antecedentes criminais.
articles.body:
Imagens que circulam nas redes sociais mostram o momento em que um pai e sua filha, ambos mexicanos, são detidos por agentes de imigração em um aeroporto de Seattle, nos Estados Unidos.

A abordagem ocorreu no sábado (21), quando Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza e Sofia Hernandez Mejia embarcavam para a Califórnia. Eles viajavam para participar de uma cerimônia de batismo de um familiar, segundo a advogada dos dois.

A prisão ocorreu na ponte de embarque de um voo da Alaska Airlines, no Aeroporto Internacional de Seattle-Tacoma, e provocou tumulto diante de outros passageiros.

Um dos vídeos, registrado por passageiros que embarcavam na aeronave, mostra um agente usando jaqueta sem identificação e calça cáqui, enquanto tenta conter uma pessoa no chão. (veja acima)

As gravações tiveram grande repercussão nas redes sociais. O voo, que tinha como destino Los Angeles, sofreu atraso.

Segundo Olia Catala, advogada do pai e da filha, ambos estão solicitando asilo nos EUA, onde vivem desde 2015.

“Eles fizeram tudo corretamente e são pessoas instruídas”, disse a advogada. “Ela cursou faculdade, universidade, trabalhou para uma organização sem fins lucrativos. Nenhum deles tem antecedentes criminais. Então, é simplesmente de partir o coração.”

Pai e filha presos pelo ICE nos EUA estavam viajando para um batismo; VÍDEO mostra abordagem — Foto: Reprodução

O Serviço de Imigração e Alfândega dos Estados Unidos (ICE) informou, em comunicado, que Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza foi detido por permanecer no país após o vencimento de seu visto, “em violação às leis de nossa nação”.

O ICE acrescentou que, durante a abordagem, Sofia Hernandez Mejia “jogou café quente nos agentes”. Segundo a agência, ela também permaneceu nos EUA após o vencimento de seu visto e poderá ser acusada de agredir um agente federal.

A advogada Olia Catala afirma que Mejia é casada com um cidadão americano e já havia apresentado documentos para regularizar sua situação migratória. O marido acompanhava a mulher e o pai dela quando ambos foram detidos no sábado. Ele não foi preso.

Segundo Catala, pai e filha ficaram detidos em um centro de detenção de imigrantes do ICE em Tacoma, no estado de Washington.

A advogada também afirmou que Mejia segurava um copo de café no momento da abordagem e contestou a versão das autoridades de que a mulher teria jogado a bebida nos agentes. “Quando alguém avança contra você, você acaba derrubando um copo de café."

“Foi uma confusão enorme e, sinceramente, se alguém corre ou avança na sua direção sem estar usando uniforme, você não sabe quem é aquela pessoa”, afirmou. “Houve muito pânico, caos, sem que ninguém soubesse o que estava acontecendo.”

A Alaska Airlines informou que não foi avisada previamente pelos agentes do ICE sobre a operação, realizada em um fim de semana de grande movimento nos aeroportos americanos, às vésperas do feriado de Ação de Graças.

O ICE intensificou as prisões em aeroportos desde o verão no Hemisfério Norte, especialmente de pessoas que, segundo a agência, permaneceram nos EUA após o vencimento de seus vistos.

A companhia aérea também afirmou que trabalha com a Autoridade Portuária de Seattle, responsável pela administração do aeroporto, para verificar se os protocolos foram seguidos. Além disso, informou que apresentou suas preocupações “diretamente às autoridades competentes”.

Em comunicado, a Autoridade Portuária de Seattle afirmou que a prisão foi angustiante tanto para a família envolvida quanto para os demais passageiros. O órgão também informou que buscaria esclarecimentos junto às autoridades federais para entender melhor o ocorrido.

O governador de Washington, Bob Ferguson, do Partido Democrata, também criticou a abordagem. Ele classificou as táticas do ICE como “profundamente contrárias aos valores americanos” e defendeu a extinção da agência.

“O vídeo é horrível e assustador”, disse Ferguson durante uma entrevista coletiva no sábado, ao lado de líderes sindicais e autoridades locais eleitas.

articles.summary: Disputa entre presidente e vice-presidente ameaça aprofundar a crise no país, enquanto o adiamento das eleições prolonga as incertezas sobre o futuro político do país.
articles.body:
Quinze anos após sua independência, o Sudão do Sul enfrenta uma grave escalada de violência e um cenário de incerteza política. Com mais de 16 milhões de habitantes vivendo sob ameaça de fome, surtos de doenças e descolamentos forçados, o país mais jovem do mundo lida com ataques a unidades de saúde, aumento de violência sexual e confrontos armados entre grupos de oposição e forças do governo.

Para aprofundar a crise, as primeiras eleições gerais da história do país foram adiadas, enquanto o presidente Salva Kiir se mantém no poder em meio a rivalidades étnicas e disputas pelo controle das valiosas reservas de petróleo.

Neste episódio, Natuza Nery conversa com o jornalista Pedro Borges, editor da agência de notícias Alma Preta, que relata diretamente da capital, Juba, os bastidores da sua apuração no país e a situação de vulnerabilidade da população civil. Ela também conversa com César Augusto Chidozie, advogado e apresentador do podcast África em Pauta. César analisa as origens históricas da crise desde o período de colonização britânica e o racha político entre o presidente Salva Kiir e seu rival Riek Machar.

articles.title: Tempestade no RS: 97% da população de Tupanciretã está fora de casa | G1
articles.standfirst: Defesa Civil contabiliza 44 municípios afetados. Em Tupanciretã, ventos chegaram a 114 km/h e mais de 19 mil moradores tiveram que deixar suas residências após estragos.
articles.summary: Tempestade no RS deixa cinco mortos e 19 mil desalojados em Tupanciretã, onde ventos de 114 km/h atingiram 97% dos moradores e danificaram milhares de residências.
articles.body:
Mais de 19 mil pessoas seguem fora de casa após a supercélula que deixou um rastro de destruição em Tupanciretã , na Região Central do Rio Grande do Sul. O número corresponde a 97% da população do município, que tem 20.005 pessoas , segundo o Censo de 2022 do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

Uma estação do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) registrou rajadas de vento de 114 km/h durante o temporal.

A Defesa Civil do estado confirmou cinco mortes em decorrência do temporal . O boletim divulgado na manhã desta segunda-feira (23) também aponta mais de 7,7 mil residências destelhadas e 265 feridos na cidade.

Ao todo, 44 municípios registraram danos devido a chuva que atingiu o RS entre sexta-feira (20) e o sábado (21). O levantamento estadual também aponta danos em 29 escolas, três estabelecimentos de saúde, quatro órgãos de infraestrutura pública e 19 estabelecimentos comerciais ou de serviços.

Além de Tupanciretã, as cidades mais atingidas foram São Domingos do Sul, onde um vendaval afetou 1,4 mil pessoas; Lagoa Vermelha, que teve 820 pessoas prejudicadas e 200 casas com danos; e Jari, onde 250 casas foram danificadas.

articles.title: 'Me considero filho', diz médico que fez parto da madrasta no TO | G1
articles.standfirst: Ginecologista e obstetra, Ridelson Miranda acompanhou a gestação desde as primeiras semanas. Família é do Tocantins e registros do nascimento repercutiram na internet.
articles.summary: Ginecologista e obstetra, Ridelson Miranda acompanhou a gestação desde as primeiras semanas. Família é do Tocantins e registros do nascimento repercutiram na internet.
articles.body:
O médico Ridelson Miranda viveu um momento incomum enquanto obstetra e responsável pela realização da cesariana de sua madrasta, em um hospital particular em Palmas . A experiência de ajudar a trazer ao mundo o próprio irmão teve um significado especial para ele, que afirma ter uma relação de afeto e proximidade com a paciente.

"Sou enteado dela e me considero seu filho de coração. Ela sempre cuidou muito de mim. No dia em que Rubens Miguel nasceu, fui eu quem fez a cesariana, com meu pai ao meu lado", relatou.

A cesariana estava agendada, mas Wildeany Rodrigues, de 44 anos, entrou em trabalho de parto antes da data prevista. Com a mudança nos planos, a família se mobilizou para realizar o procedimento. A cirurgia foi acompanhada pela irmã e pelo Ricardo Miranda, que também é médico e atuou como auxiliar na cirurgia. O registro do nascimento repercutiu nas redes sociais.

Wildeany fazia acompanhamento preventivo com o enteado, que também é ginecologista, e apresentava irregularidades no ciclo menstrual. Isso tornava a gravidez improvável.

Ao lado do pai na sala de parto, médico realizou a cesariana do irmão recém-nascido — Foto: Ridelson Miranda/Arquivo pessoal

Após o nascimento, Ridelson publicou fotos do momento em uma rede social com a legenda: “O dia que meu irmão veio ao mundo pelas minhas mãos”. O parto foi realizado em abril, mas Ridelson Miranda compartilhou os registros apenas no mês de novembro.

Em uma sequência de fotos, Ridelson registrou os bastidores do nascimento, desde a preparação da equipe, com vestimentas cirúrgicas, máscaras e toucas, até o momento em que o recém-nascido foi colocado no colo de Wildeany, logo após o parto. Ele também destacou o orgulho de dividir o campo cirúrgico com a maior referência profissional de sua vida.

"Quando eu lembrar daquele dia, vou lembrar de me preparar para a cirurgia ao lado do meu pai, um médico que sempre admirei, e de vê-lo depois com o Miguel no colo. Ainda fico imaginando o que foi, para ele, ajudar um filho a trazer outro filho ao mundo", destacou o médico.

Ridelson havia participado dos partos dos próprios filhos e do nascimento da sobrinha. Trazer o irmão ao mundo, no entanto, representou uma experiência inédita para toda a equipe hospitalar. Com a chegada do bebê, os filhos do obstetra, Mariana e Ricardo, agora têm um tio cerca de dez anos mais novo que eles.

"O comentário que mais se repetiu foi que ninguém ali se lembrava de ter visto uma situação assim. Dessa vez, era meu próprio irmão que eu estava ajudando a nascer. Fica a gratidão por ter vivido com a minha família um momento que eu jamais teria imaginado", concluiu.

articles.title: Princesa dos Campos inaugura unidade de Cargas em Maringá | G1
articles.standfirst: Com 1.800 m², estrutura amplia a capacidade operacional e fortalece os serviços logísticos da empresa no norte do Paraná.
articles.summary: Com 1.800 m², estrutura amplia a capacidade operacional e fortalece os serviços logísticos da empresa no norte do Paraná.
articles.body:
A infraestrutura logística é um dos principais pilares para ampliar a eficiência no transporte de cargas. Atenta a essa demanda, a Princesa dos Campos inaugurou o novo armazém para a sua operação de cargas e encomendas - Prinex em Maringá (PR), fortalecendo sua estrutura em um dos principais polos econômicos do Paraná.

A estrutura no norte do estado, tem localização estratégica e de fácil acesso para a operação diária. Além disso, a inauguração do novo espaço está diretamente ligada à importância da e um terminal adequado para as etapas de recebimento, movimentação e expedição de mercadorias.

Presente em Maringá há 31 anos, a Princesa dos Campos começou as suas atividades na região com um terminal de 150m². Em 2010, avançou para uma estrutura de 990m² e neste ano, está alocada em uma sede com 1.800m². O Grupo conta ainda com uma frota de aproximadamente 350 veículos para o atendimento da área de cargas.

A cidade de Maringá é um grande conector logístico com o restante do Paraná e com o interior de São Paulo, visto a sua posição estratégica e vasta abrangência. E não para por aí. Segundo dados do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), Maringá é o terceiro município mais populoso do estado, com população estimada em 432.635 pessoas. Além disso, com base no boletim Radar Paraná, lançado pela Casa Civil do PR, Maringá registrou um Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) de R$ 27,817 bilhões em 2025, ocupando o 5º lugar do ranking no estado e a 55ª posição na economia nacional.

De acordo com Renan Fragoso Tanaka, Diretor de Negócios e Operações de Cargas, a inauguração do novo terminal mostra como a empresa acompanha esse crescimento contínuo da região norte do Paraná, mantendo a garantia dos seus serviços. “Seguimos firmes no propósito de entregar as melhores soluções logísticas para os clientes, reforçando nossa presença nesta região, que, visto o histórico comprovado de crescimento consistente, posiciona a nossa marca como a melhor opção de transporte de cargas para as empresas” , destaca.

Fachada Princesa dos Campos. — Foto: Divulgação/Princesa dos Campos.

A operação de Cargas do Grupo Princesa dos Campos, é uma solução logística inteligente que utiliza tanto o bagageiro dos ônibus quanto os caminhões para o transporte de mercadorias. Sua operação atende desde grandes clientes, que necessitam garantir o abastecimento de regiões amplas e pulverizadas, até empresas de menor porte, com demandas e rotas mais específicas.

Diariamente, as mercadorias são coletadas no local solicitado e são entregues no destino final, com garantia de previsibilidade e rastreamento em todo o percurso. Esse trabalho ocorre, visto o motorista possuir um aplicativo conectado ao Sistema de Gerenciamento de Transporte (TMS), em que ali ele registra a coleta no sistema. Neste registro, a mercadoria recebe uma etiqueta e a partir daí, é monitorada em todo trajeto. Na prática, o cliente tem visibilidade e informação em todo trajeto e é informado de qualquer ocorrência que eventualmente possa ocorrer na rota.

“ Para garantir essa visibilidade ao longo do trajeto, investimos muito em tecnologia. Temos sistemas conectados que recebem informações do motorista, mas que também estão integrados aos nossos times de filiais e de backoffice, os quais ficam de prontidão para tratar qualquer problema que haja no envio”, explica Tanaka.

Ainda segundo o Diretor, o grande diferencial do Prinex Cargas não se resume em apenas conseguir atender os clientes através dos caminhões, mas sim, o prazo de entrega, que supre todo o Paraná em até 24h. “ Além da capilaridade em nossas rotas, conseguimos utilizar nossos bagageiros de ônibus para alavancar o nível de serviço. Sabemos que o prazo de entrega no mercado atual significa faturamento para o vendedor/embarcador, e nós queremos ser um aliado dessas empresas, com toda a expertise que o Grupo Princesa dos Campos apresenta em mais de 90 anos de história”, conclui.

A sede do Prinex Cargas em Maringá está localizada na Rodovia PR 317, nº 5283 - Gleba Ribeirão Pinguim. O horário de atendimento é de Segunda à Sábado, das 06h às 21h. O telefone para contato é o canal oficial da Princesa dos Campos: 0800 42 10000.

articles.title: Eduardo Moscovis apresenta espetáculo 'O Motociclista no Globo da Morte' em Salvador | G1
articles.standfirst: Com texto de Leonardo Netto e direção de Rodrigo Portella, o monólogo propõe uma reflexão sobre a violência humana ao explorar as fronteiras entre vítima e algoz, civilidade e selvageria.
articles.summary: Com texto de Leonardo Netto e direção de Rodrigo Portella, o monólogo propõe uma reflexão sobre a violência humana ao explorar as fronteiras entre vítima e algoz, civilidade e selvageria.
articles.body:
Ator Eduardo Moscovis apresenta espetáculo 'O Motociclista no Globo da Morte' em Salvador — Foto: Divulgação

O ator Eduardo Moscovis apresenta o espetáculo “ O Motociclista no Globo da Morte” , nos dias 28 e 29 de novembro, às 20h, no Teatro Faresi, em Salvador . Os ingressos custam entre R$ 25 e R$ 180, e estão disponíveis na internet e na bilheteria do local.

Com texto de Leonardo Netto e direção de Rodrigo Portella, o monólogo propõe uma reflexão sobre a violência humana ao explorar as fronteiras entre vítima e algoz, civilidade e selvageria.

A história narra a vida aparentemente correta e pacífica de um homem que, diante de determinadas circunstâncias, pode se aproximar daquele que considera seu oposto. A partir desse conflito, o espetáculo questiona os limites da violência e a capacidade humana de reproduzir atos extremo s.

Segundo a organização do espetáculo, a inspiração para o texto surgiu depois que Leonardo Netto assistiu, em uma rede social, a um vídeo de extrema violência. A experiência despertou questionamentos sobre o que leva alguém a cometer esse tipo de ato e também a filmá-lo, publicá-lo e consumi-lo.

Em cena, Eduardo Moscovis conduz sozinho a narrativa, em seu segundo monólogo teatral. O primeiro foi “O Livro”, de Newton Moreno, apresentado em 2011, com direção de Christiane Jatahy. O ator destaca a força do texto e a identificação com o protagonista como aspectos que o mobilizaram durante o processo de criação.

O título da peça funciona como uma metáfora da iminência do desastre. Assim como os motociclistas que circulam dentro do globo da morte, os personagens parecem viver em permanente tentativa de escapar de uma catástrofe.

A montagem é o quinto espetáculo produzido por Eduardo Moscovis. O trabalho rendeu ao ator o Prêmio Shell de Melhor Ator, considerado um dos mais tradicionais reconhecimentos das artes cênicas brasileiras e o primeiro de sua carreira.

articles.title: Psychology says people who make their bed every morning, even when staying in a hotel or someone else's home, may find comfort in familiar routines, a sense of order and the feeling of starting the day with one small task completed
articles.summary: Some people cannot leave their bed unmade, even when they are staying in a hotel, in a holiday apartment for just one night.
articles.body: Some people cannot leave their bed unmade, even when they are staying in a hotel, in a holiday apartment for just one night. They wake up, fold the duvet, straighten the pillows and make sure everything looks neat before heading out.For them, making the bed is part of getting the day started. And the habit often travels with them. Whether they are staying in a relative's home, a holiday apartment or a hotel room, they still feel the urge to straighten the bedding before leaving.It may look like a small domestic habit, but there are interesting psychological reasons why some people stick to it.Does making the bed give people a sense of achievement?There is also the satisfaction of finishing something. Making a bed is a small, visible task with a clear result. The sheets are straight, the pillows are arranged and the room looks a little tidier than it did a few minutes ago.This connects with the psychological idea of task completion. Finishing even a minor activity can give people a sense of progress, particularly at the beginning of the day.In a hotel, this behaviour is perhaps more interesting because the person has no real responsibility to do it. The room belongs to someone else, and housekeeping is likely to take care of it. Yet they still make the effort.For some, the reward is not praise or recognition. It is simply the satisfaction of seeing the task done. They may feel more comfortable leaving a room that looks organised, even if they are going to return only in the evening.Is it linked to a need for order?People have different preferences when it comes to their surroundings. Some are perfectly comfortable with an unmade bed, clothes on a chair and a few belongings scattered around. Others find a messy room distracting.For the latter group, making the bed may be one way of creating visual order. A neatly arranged bed can change how an entire room looks, even when the rest of the space remains untouched.Research has examined how people respond to their physical surroundings and how environmental order, clutter and visual distractions can influence mood and attention.Why does the habit continue even when nobody is watching?This is perhaps the most revealing part of the behaviour. When people make their beds at home, they may do it because they share the room with someone else or want the house to look presentable. But in a hotel room, there is usually no such expectation.Behavioural psychology explains that repeated actions in familiar situations can gradually become habits. Once a person gets out of bed, straightening the sheets may happen almost without conscious decision-making.There may also be a personal standard involved. Some people like to leave a space as they found it, or even a little better. Others simply dislike the thought of returning to an untidy room after a long day of sightseeing, meetings or travel.And not everyone who does this attaches a deeper meaning to the action. Sometimes, a habit is just a habit.Does making your bed say something about your personality?It can offer a small glimpse into someone's preferences, but it cannot tell us everything about their personality.It would be wrong to assume that they are more productive, disciplined or successful than someone who leaves their bed untouched. There is no established psychological rule that links this one habit to overall personality or achievement.Perhaps the simplest explanation is also the most relatable. Travel changes the surroundings, the schedule and the usual comforts of home. But making the bed is one small thing that remains familiar.And for someone who likes starting the day with a tidy room, it takes only a minute to bring a little bit of home into a hotel room.You use AI every day. articles.title: Who is Alberto Feijoo, the conservative seeking to become Spain’s new PM?
articles.summary: The former career civil servant hopes to lead his Popular Party to victory in November 29 elections.
articles.body:
With the confidence of a composed manager, Alberto Nunez Feijoo declared he knows how to run public infrastructure and handle crises as he made his final pitch to Spanish voters in a televised debate last week. Minutes earlier, the conservative Popular Party (PP) leader had vehemently accused Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez of being a “gift to people smugglers”.

The manager had morphed into a far-right politician.

Thursday’s showdown – the last between the two leading contenders in Spain’s November 29 elections – underscored the balancing act that has defined Feijoo’s campaign, split between reassuring moderate voters while sharpening his attacks on Sanchez to keep voters from drifting to the far right.

“You could see right there the two Feijoos,” said Oriol Bartomeus Bayes, a political scientist at the Autonomous University of Barcelona.

Opinion polls put the PP ahead of Sanchez’s Socialist Party (PSOE) but short of an outright majority. The far-right Vox party, which is polling third, could provide the parliamentary votes Feijoo would need to govern.

Feijoo, 65, was a career civil servant before entering politics. Born in the northwestern province of Ourense, he held senior posts in Galicia’s health service and went on to run Spain’s state postal service.

He led Galicia’s regional government from 2009 to 2022, winning four consecutive outright majorities. During that time, he earned a reputation as a capable administrator with a measured public style.

When the PP chose Feijoo as its leader in 2022, his election was seen as a victory for the party’s moderates. But he inherited a problem familiar to centre-right parties elsewhere in Europe: A challenger on his right was drawing voters away from his own party. As the PP competed with Vox, Feijoo hardened his language on immigration and stepped up his attacks on the ruling Socialists over alleged corruption.

“The moderates won by electing Feijoo, but at the end, he evolved to embrace a more radical discourse on corruption, immigration, abortion and in his rhetoric against the PSOE, accusing it of being an immoral and ‘indecent’ party,” Bayes said.

That shift was on display after the July border crisis in Ceuta , a Spanish enclave bordering Morocco, when tens of thousands of people crossed into Spanish territory. Feijoo seized the moment and harshly criticised Sanchez’s handling of the situation.

The PP has traditionally called for stronger border controls while acknowledging the importance of foreign labour to Spain’s economy, which in 2025 under the current Socialist government grew by 2.6 percent, nearly twice the European average. But the PP position has recently evolved into pledges to ban mass regularisations of undocumented immigrants and calls for tougher criteria on who may enjoy certain benefits, including length of residence and social security contributions. Vox, meanwhile, has made deportations and what it calls “remigration” a central campaign pledge.

That tougher stance comes as the PP is chasing its own voters who are seeking a sharper ideological alternative compared with what they perceive as a more cautious and technocratic PP. Polling by Ipsos suggested up to 20 percent of people who voted for the PP in the 2023 elections intended to vote for Vox in next weekend’s voting.

In the 2023 elections, Feijoo’s PP won 137 seats, more than any other party. But while it already had Vox’s backing, the two parties together fell four votes short of the 176 needed for an absolute majority to govern. Sanchez, whose party had come second with 121 seats, managed to strike a coalition deal with far-left groups and secure the support of separatist Catalan and Basque parties that helped him secure the premiership.

This time around, things could be different.

Vox is projected to win up to 18 percent of the vote and 63 seats, nearly double its 2023 results. With the PP tipped to have 127 seats, the far-right party potentially holds the balance of power as an alliance between them could lead to a comfortable majority of 190 seats, 14 more than what is needed to secure an absolute majority. For its part, the PSOE is projected to win 119 seats.

Feijoo has said he would prefer the PP govern alone with parliamentary support from Vox, but he has left open the possibility of a formal coalition with the far-right party.

A former fringe player in Spanish politics, Vox has grown to establish itself as a mainstream political force, already governing together with the PP in four regions: Andalusia, Aragon, Castile and Leon, and Extremadura.

The regional deals offer a glimpse of where the two parties might find common ground at the national level – and where they could clash. One of the clearest divides is over gender-based violence. Last year, the PP joined other parties in renewing a cross-party agreement against gender-based violence first adopted in 2017. The revised pact sets out more than 400 measures to prevent violence against women and improve support and protection for survivors and their children. Vox was the only party to vote against it, arguing that domestic violence laws should apply regardless of the victim’s sex.

The PP and Vox found more room for compromise over who should qualify for regional benefits and housing in Andalusia. Their regional coalition deal gives priority to applicants with longstanding ties to Andalusia or Spain. Criteria such as years of municipal registration and a record of social security contributions leave room for foreign residents with legal status to qualify. The deal also calls for excluding migrants from regular social benefits and services with an exception for life-threatening emergencies.

Regional joint governance has made the notion of a national agreement with Vox easier for PP voters to imagine, according to Matteo Re, a professor at Rey Juan Carlos University in Madrid.

“The PP has brought Vox into the mainstream. They are governing together in four autonomous regions, and in doing so, they have led both their own base and the rest of Spain to accept the idea that, ultimately, they will form a government with them, something they had failed to achieve in 2023,” Re said. The regional deals have also allowed the PP to show its voters what governing alongside Vox looks like with the conservatives still in charge, he said.

However Feijoo has been careful to not lose his centrist appeal. A deadly train crash last month in the central Spanish province of Toledo, less than a year after another train tragedy on the same track, gave the conservative leader a chance to return to more familiar ground , reorienting his rhetoric towards the party’s moderate base and undecided voters.

“After the train crash, he saw the possibility of appearing as a managerial leader and moved the campaign to discuss issues such as transportation, infrastructure and security. … These are topics where he is more comfortable than in the radical ideological fight,” Bayes said.

On the foreign policy front, Feijoo is expected to distance himself from Sanchez if elected.

The PSOE leader has stood out on the global stage by adopting open-border policies when the rest of Europe is closing up, resisting the push for NATO allies to spend 5 percent of their gross domestic products on defence, standing up to United States President Donald Trump and calling Israel’s war in Gaza a genocide.

Sanchez has also branded Spain under his leadership a “beacon” in a world increasingly being dominated by far-right movements seeking to undercut social progress. At home, his government moved to regularise more than a million undocumented immigrants. And at last week’s debate, the prime minister rejected proposals backed by some European governments to set up deportation centres outside the EU.

But under a PP-led government, Spain is likely to dance to a different tune. Feijoo has so far declined to commit to the 5 percent spending on defence but has promised to strengthen ties with the US.

The PP also wants to maintain military and other support for Ukraine and pursue a more balanced relationship with Morocco and Algeria. Its manifesto frames Spain’s southern border as a European priority and calls for joint European defence purchases.

“They are staunch Atlanticists and pro-European,” Re said, noting, however, that the PP’s election campaign “is entirely self-absorbed and revels in its own navel-gazing”.

Feijoo himself summed up the message in Thursday’s debate when he urged, “less talk about Trump, more about trains”.

articles.title: On the streets with the French Black Block ultra left protesters
articles.summary: The BBC meets the far-left protesters French President Emmanuel Macron says are trying to bring down the Republic.
articles.body:
France is in turmoil. Crippling public debt, a "lame-duck" president with six months left in office, and massive social unrest - sparked by student protests which have erupted into looting and violence.

This Saturday marked the sixth weekend in a row of demos against soaring prices, worsening public services and alleged police brutality. Violence by protesters is down on last month but still present.

President Emmanuel Macron has publicly blamed riots on "delinquents" and "ultra-left groups" whose aim, he says, is to bring down the French Republic.

That's quite a claim – and one that needs examining.

The unrest in France has become a political football ahead of key presidential and parliamentary elections next year. The left in France blames the centre and right for the cost-of-living crisis that's making French people so upset and angry. They blame the hard left for fomenting violence (which they deny). While the nationalist right pledges, if elected, it will return order and security to France's streets.

So, who exactly are these "ultra-left" groups Macron speaks of? And how organised and dangerous are they?

It's infamously hard to speak to members of the radical left. They don't much like what they call mainstream media. We're viewed as part of an establishment many of them despise.

My best bet was to head out into the protests and try to approach people dressed in all black and ski masks or balaclavas (worn, they say, to hide their identity from police). It's a quasi-uniform associated with left-wing rioters or disruptors, known as the Black Block.

You see them at demos all over Europe. In France, they tend to appear from city side streets, as daytime protests are dying down, dusk is falling and riot police begin to emerge in full force.

French intelligence drastically underestimated the outpouring of anger, looting and destruction following protests last month. More than 1,000 police officers were reportedly injured, young protesters had bones broken and two reportedly lost a hand in altercations with police armed with stun grenades. Le Monde newspaper has an article it is constantly updating to investigate a rising number of reports of protester injuries. The French Insurers Federation estimates damages to shops and private property on 17 October alone - the day of the biggest riots - came to around €207m (£175.5m).

Since then, the French authorities are trying to tightly manage demos. Police presence is heavy. Protesters say heavy handed.

Towards the end of one of the protests this month, we saw would-be rioters vastly outnumbered, glass bottles and homemade paint bombs at the ready to throw at police. They were no match for the batons, stun grenades and tear gas the officers had to hand.

As we were being forcefully kettled in by police, I tried to talk to would-be rioters. Few wanted to engage but I then met 18-year-old Nas (not his real name) and friends. They would only speak to me if they could hide their identity. This was to avoid police detection, they said.

Milling, you could say provocatively, by baton-at-the-ready police – they seemed to fit a radical-left rioter stereotype.

"How can you justify the violence?" I ask them.

"Without violence, you don't achieve anything," one of them tells me. "It's the only way to get our voices heard."

"We come from an area with a bad reputation. Our schools are a mess. Our teachers quit. You need qualifications to get a decent job. There is supposed to be equality in France. We won't give up our fight."

These young men, we discover, come from the sprawling housing estates common on French city outskirts - the banlieues - associated with deprivation, unrest and second or third generation immigrant families.

They weren't politicised or organised by the radical left, they insisted. Just angry.

Earlier, I had spotted two hard-left student activists, standing masked on top of a bus shelter, above the thronging crowd of protesters waving banners sporting the red anarchist sign and the symbol for the Antifa (anti-fascist) movement.

I put it to them that France has a proud tradition and respect for the right to protest but that the country has been horrified by the violence it's seen over the last weeks.

They were keen to downplay the rioting but - again – would only speak if they could remain anonymous.

"Violence ends up reflecting badly on our movements. We don't like it. But what's a smashed shop window compared to police using stun guns on protesting school kids? Also, people [in France] are regularly going cold and hungry. They're losing faith in this society."

How could they believe violence would bring about a juster society, I wondered?

They shrug off my question. In France, these days, the real violence is state violence, they say.

French intelligence estimates there are 5,000 "ultra-left" activists in the country.

Anticapitalist Starflix (that's his codename) counts himself as one of them. The 17-year-old is also a member of the violent Black Block movement. We'd arranged to meet on the edge of the protest, by a narrow canal.

Fearful about being apprehended by police, he asked to remain anonymous.

He showed me a couple of homemade paint-bombs - eggshells filled with paint and sealed with medical tape that he throws at police officers. He carries them in his rucksack, wrapped in a royal blue Italia football shirt.

"We throw the paint bombs at the visors on riot police helmets, so they have to lift them up in order to see and that makes them suffer their own tear gas that they've sprayed at us," he tells me.

"We pick up stones and rocks too. Anything we find on the streets of Paris, to throw."

I put it to him that he and others in the Black Block are causing a lot of problems on French streets: damaging businesses, hurting police officers, destroying the demos for peaceful protesters. What is he trying to achieve?

As he's under 18, his parents give us permission to speak to him. They share his politics, Starflix tells me, but not all rioters - masked and dressed in black as he is - do.

"The Black Block isn't a single organisation. It's a technique. Some of us use violence to get government reform. I want to bring about a revolution.

"Other people are opportunists who use anonymity to steal things. When we all wear the same clothes, it makes it harder for police to identify us."

When I ask if he is scared he might get hurt or arrested, he admits he is but says what frightens him more is the thought that society might not change.

Social media plays a huge role in the riots. Starflix tells me he and his friends use Signal and Telegram to arrange to meet at protests.

There are numerous websites and Instagram profiles, mainly hosted by left-wing organisations, offering tips for protesters and rioters, such as: keep your phone at home so police can't track you, cover your face to avoid being identified and emulate martial arts expert Bruce Lee and "be like water" - appearing and disappearing into crowds. That's advice passed on by the Hong Kong protesters eight years ago.

While not formally organising the protests or violence with these posts, could the fact groups host this information online be viewed as a kind of incitement or manipulation of youngsters whose feelings are running so high in France?

All the young rioters I spoke to insist they are not being herded or directed, but is there something bigger behind what's happening?

It takes our team a long time, but they manage to find a seasoned activist with the Black Block who would speak to us. I put to him Macron's assertion that the ultra left has organised groups that aim to bring down the French Republic. Is that true?

"It's totally false of the authorities to say we are all organised. And the intelligence services know it," the activist scoffs. "It's a manipulation of the French public to make them think there is an enemy within."

"Basically, people turn up to a protest, get dressed in black and do their own thing. The uniting factor is rage and not just in France. You see the same rage [in protests] in Italy, Germany, Spain. It's exploding by itself."

I ask if the anti-capitalist presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon and his France Unbowed party (LFI) are somehow linked to the violence. They are present at most protests, supporters handing out campaign pamphlets to the chanting crowds.

But the activist denies this, telling me Mélenchon is "a capitalist because he's part of the system". He says the LFI and the trade unions try to "calm" unrest, while he believes things need to be "stepped up a notch".

Why had he decided to talk to us, I ask - does he want to collapse the French government?

"I just want to say we don't love violence. I don't want to destroy France. We want to destroy a system that is a capitalist system, of course, but to change the society in a way that we think will be better for the most people, for more people.

"More and more find it hard to make ends meet. In the countryside, people can't even afford to fill their tank with petrol."

You have to leave the city, heading out into the gloriously autumnal French countryside, to meet some of the more organised, hardcore elements of the ultra left.

This is a world of eco activism and known saboteurs. One man remains in police custody linked to the fire during protests at Limoges Town Hall last month . The devastated, yet somehow still elegant, 19th century building has become a symbol of the current state France appears to be in. An acrid smell still hangs in the air one month on.

The 34-year-old arson suspect, who insists he's innocent, comes from a hamlet near Limoges, known for its anarchist, environmentalist community. His father, a fellow activist, is also known to French intelligence. We approached the father and the suspect's lawyer for comment. They didn't want to speak.

Instead, we met a 39-year-old father of one, a local full-time ultra-left activist for more than two decades. Like the other individuals we spoke to for this investigation, he would only talk to us on condition he could remain anonymous.

"We were all shocked by the [town hall] fire – even as we watched it happen in front of us - but it's our duty to take action," he tells me.

"I can't leave this world to my son in the state that it's in. Look how military vehicles and brute force are used by the state against our young students.

"It's amazing the people haven't taken up arms against them. Do we need a policeman killed in order for the state to listen?"

"As a child, I was educated with French values – liberty, equality, fraternity - but when I look at the social injustice in the world now, I'm disgusted. As a father, I can't let this go on. If I have to, I would take a bullet to protect the youth of this country."

These are dangerous-sounding words - but the radical left doesn't appear to be big, armed or united enough to seriously threaten France.

We repeatedly approached French intelligence. They didn't want to comment. A sign perhaps of the huge sensitivity of the current situation, especially with France hurtling towards an extremely charged presidential election.

But Michel Klein, a recently retired former police commissioner, told me he didn't think the radical left posed a serious threat to the French state.

"I believe there is a will from the radical left and the anarchists to try and destroy the Republic but they obviously don't have the means to do it," he told me.

He sees no risk of civil war in France (a possibility you hear some in the country discuss these days) but he identified a rising risk of clashes between far-left and far-right groups ahead of the presidential election.

Polls currently predict a run-off in the vote between nationalist candidate Marine Le Pen and anticapitalist Mélenchon.

Far-right vigilante groups have begun appearing on the edge of protests in a number of cities across France to "protect French streets", they say.

The popular hard-left presidential candidate Mélenchon attends most demos, his supporters handing political pamphlets to the chanting crowds, but he denies any links with violence.

France is so polarised, there's little sign next year's presidential vote will calm things. This turbulent mix of left and right, social and political unrest, feels like a perfect storm.

Europe's youth is on the march - but does anything actually unite them?

articles.title: As Syria-EU talks progress, diplomats fear focus will be on repatriation
articles.summary: Syria and the EU are in talks on trade and political ties, but migration will likely be the key issue for discussion.
articles.body:
Officials from Syria and the European Union are working on a deal to normalise relations after a 15-year suspension. But current and former European diplomats have told Al Jazeera they fear that growing right-wing sentiment in Europe could see efforts to repatriate Syrians and immigration being prioritised over other key issues, such as human rights.

Syrian and EU officials hope that a deal with the new government will lead to stronger trade and political relations, after a suspension following then-President Bashar al-Assad’s brutal crackdown on protesters in 2011.

With al-Assad’s regime overthrown and a government led by President Ahmed al-Sharaa seeking closer relations with Europe, there is an opportunity for diplomatic and trade relations to resume.

“The aim is to give Europe and Syria a framework for trade, political dialogue and closer cooperation as soon as possible,” Kaja Kallas, vice president of the European Commission, said in a statement on November 16. “Syria needs investment and a successful transition.”

Analysts and diplomats told Al Jazeera that Syria’s priority in the talks was the removal of lingering EU sanctions. Brussels is largely focused on the repatriation of Syrians, with more than a million fleeing to Europe during the Syrian war between 2011 and 2024. But they added that these issues must be managed carefully to avoid piling pressure on Syria as it continues to rebuild after the war and decades of dictatorship.

“The migration issue is a big issue in Europe today,” Iyad Jaber, the Damascus-based head of Middle East at Timios & Co and former French diplomat of Syrian origin, told Al Jazeera. “Especially with right-wing and far-right wing [parties] taking more political space, it is moving political speech on migration.”

The first cooperation agreement between Europe and Syria was signed in 1978 by the EU’s predecessor, the European Economic Community (EEC), when Hafez al-Assad was Syria’s president. The agreement was focused on the economic and social development of Syria and a deepening of ties between the two parties.

In 2008, the EU-Syria Association Agreement was proposed but never signed by either side, largely due to concerns over the Assad government’s record on human rights. In 2011, when the government brutally repressed a popular uprising, the EU suspended ties with Syria.

During that time, the EU moved its diplomatic mission to Beirut and imposed sanctions on the Assad regime, freezing its assets and imposing travel bans on key officials.

Since the overthrow of the Assad regime, the EU has aimed to revive relations with the country. It lifted all economic sanctions on Syria last year, though some dual-use export controls and state institutions remain sanctioned.

In January, Brussels announced a two-year funding package of 620 million euros ($680m) for Syria and in May the EU held its first high-level political dialogue with Syria, which aimed to revive bilateral relations.

The EU’s diplomatic service prepared a discussion paper outlining the normalisation efforts. Al Jazeera reached out to the paper’s author, but she was unavailable for comment.

Kallas said diplomats are now working through technical and legal details to finalise the agreement, which would create frameworks for free trade, political dialogue and broader cooperation between Brussels and Damascus.

Many European nations have been exploring reopening embassies or missions in Syria, diplomats told Al Jazeera, while Syrian and EU officials continue talks on normalisation and sanctions removal.

Sally Shobat, Syria’s European Affairs Directorate at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, met Jonas Jonsson, head of the Middle East and North Africa Division at the European External Action Service, on Saturday, after earlier holding bilateral meetings with French, Cypriot and Belgian diplomatic officials.

Since the fall of the Assad government, Syria’s new government has worked to revive suspended relations and remove sanctions imposed on its predecessor. Many of the penalties have now been removed and relations with many countries, notably members of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) and the United States, have also improved .

EU-Syrian relations may be moving in a positive direction, but experts said there are still many legal and technical obstacles to full normalisation.

“Every country has their own foreign policy,” Zakaria al-Shmaly, a nonresident fellow at TIMEP focusing on EU-Syria relations, told Al Jazeera.

Still, Syria has tried to prove its importance to Europe in security matters, particularly in the fight against ISIL (ISIS) and as an energy transit point following global disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

“Europe needs Syria as much as Syria needs Europe,” President al-Sharaa said in Nicosia in April, after an informal meeting between Syria and EU officials.

In April, al-Sharaa proposed the Four Seas and Nine Corridors Initiative, a proposed transatlantic framework connecting the Gulf, Caspian Sea, Mediterranean Sea and Black Sea via a Syria-Turkiye pipeline and transit corridor. The proposal bypasses the Strait of Hormuz for a land pipeline through Syria, following disruptions to shipping because of the US-Israel war on Iran, which began in February.

“Every power is using Syria to undermine Iran,” al-Shmaly said.

Another key point of discussion between the EU and Syria as normalisation talks continue will be trade. Experts said Brussels will likely try to open the Syrian market to EU products, which could benefit Syrian consumers by lowering costs on certain items. However, Syrian negotiators must also consider what kind of things Syrian companies can export to the EU.

“There are not a lot of Syrian exports,” Jaber told Al Jazeera. “They are mostly agricultural and some pharmaceutical, but there are not a lot of exports and this is what the Syrians need to be careful about; otherwise, they will open the market to a lot of European products while still facing barriers and tariffs on what they can export.”

Jaber said there is also room for EU-Syrian coordination on the issue of Assad regime assets, which could be worth tens of billions of dollars and “hidden in several parts of Europe”.

In the months following a change in government in Damascus, some European states paused asylum claims for Syrians, citing that the dangers from the war and former regime were over.

Migration and the presence of refugees have been a major political issue in Europe for over a decade, particularly as a number of countries experienced a growth in far-right parties or movements.

In her comments on November 16, Kallas addressed the future of human rights in Syria and decisions taken by the Assad regime. “Everybody said that we need to engage with Syria because if we don’t engage, then this vacuum will be filled by other players,” Kallas said. “We should have clear conditionality regarding human rights. We should have also the nonrecognition of occupied Ukrainian, Georgian territories that they have recognised under Assad’s regime.”

In recent years, al-Shmaly claimed that even governments on the political centre-ground had adopted increasingly extreme policies on immigration.

Current and former European diplomats told Al Jazeera they were concerned that Europe would overly focus on repatriation in any deal with Syria, leaving human rights and other important issues by the wayside.

“Structurally, we have a rising number of member states in the EU that are led by right-wing populists who see no interest in engaging in all of Syria’s complexity and challenges,” a former European diplomat, who requested to speak on background, told Al Jazeera.

“We tend to see Syria only through the very limited lens of migration and we also wrongly perceive Syrian refugees as a burden rather than an opportunity despite the fact that the overwhelming majority of Syrian refugees have very positively contributed to the European economy and culture.”

Since the fall of the Assad government, about one million Syrians have returned home, most from neighbouring countries such as Lebanon, Turkiye and Jordan. But experts said Europe must strike a delicate balance on migration due to the slow process of rebuilding the country after years of dictatorship and war.

“As the European Union deepens ties with Syria, returns cannot become the price of that relationship,” Tariq Azeez, the International Rescue Committee’s policy, advocacy and communications coordinator, told Al Jazeera.

“Our research shows the reality many Syrians are returning to: missing services, damaged housing and conditions worse than expected, and competition over scarce resources driving tension within communities. Accelerating returns, therefore, without investing in services for everyone, returnees and those who never left alike, risks fuelling exactly the instability Europe says it wants to prevent.”

articles.title: Durrell marks progress in 100-year Highlands restoration plan
articles.summary: The wildlife charity is three years in to the rewilding project in Scotland.
articles.body:
A wildlife charity says it is already seeing signs of nature recovering just three years into a 100-year project to restore part of the Scottish Highlands.

Jersey's Durrell Wildlife Conservation Trust has recorded nearly 18,000 naturally regenerating trees and more than 1,000 species of plants and animals across its 7,500-hectare Dalnacardoch estate in the Cairngorms National Park .

The charity said it has also restored 365 hectares of damaged peatland and identified another 2,200 hectares for future work.

Durrell chief executive Rebecca Brewer said they were seeing "encouraging signs" but the project was about "much more than what we can achieve in our own lifetimes".

Durrell took on stewardship of the Dalnacardoch estate, north of Blair Atholl, in 2023 under a 100-year lease.

The conservation charity says its work focuses on restoring habitats including peatlands, native woodland and rivers, while creating jobs, training and volunteering opportunities for local communities.

Brewer said: "By restoring damaged peatlands, reducing grazing pressure and giving native woodland and wildlife the chance to recover, we can help bring this landscape back to life.

"We're laying the foundations for a landscape that future generations will see transformed, with thriving peatlands, recovering woodland and wildlife returning."

Surveys carried out in 2025 and 2026 recorded 17,828 young trees growing naturally across the estate.

Researchers also found more than 3,500 montane willows, making the estate an internationally important site for the rare mountain species.

Wildlife surveys have recorded more than 1,000 species so far, including 540 insect types. Among the findings were the rare azure hawker dragonfly and black alpine-sedge, a plant not recorded in the area since the 1980s.

Plans for the coming years include restoring parts of the River Edendon Water, improving freshwater habitats and reconnecting sections of the river with its natural floodplain.

articles.title: Search for missing Derbyshire donkey leaves autistic boy heartbroken
articles.summary: Niamh says her non-verbal son formed a bond with Gabriel, who disappeared overnight on Thursday.
articles.body:
A three-year-old autistic boy has been left "absolutely heartbroken" after a baby donkey he bonded with from birth disappeared from his family's farm in Derbyshire.

"He's gone down, his donkey isn't there and he is absolutely heartbroken," said his mother, Niamh.

The foal, named Gabriel, vanished overnight on Thursday and has not been seen since at the farm near Darley Abbey, despite searches, social media appeals and a £500 reward.

For Niamh's non-verbal son, Gabriel was more than just a pet.

Gabriel's mother was adopted from a sanctuary, which specialises in catering for Special Educational Needs and Disabilities children, making her a perfect fit for Niamh's son.

The family are particularly confused by what they believe is a theft as male donkeys - known as a jack - have little monetary value, unlike females, which are called a jenny.

Niamh said: "He is a pet, but obviously with me gifting to my little boy, he's more.

"We have a heartbroken jenny donkey which doesn't understand where her baby has gone.

"I also have a heartbroken little boy that can't comprehend what has happened, being on the spectrum and being non-verbal."

Niamh, her parents and two sisters have visited neighbouring farms and houses and put out appeals on social media in an effort to trace the donkey.

Increasing to the stress is the fact Gabriel cannot survive if left unattended.

"He should still be on his mum, like a newborn baby with the colostrum, that is what he needs," Niamh said.

"You can't just put him in a stable with some hay, he won't survive.

"Whoever has him has to know what they are doing if they are to keep him alive because he would need specialist milk.

"So this is why we are so lost, we don't have a lead, there's no update there's no nothing, just silence."

articles.title: Stoke-on-Trent school first in England to tackle loan sharks
articles.summary: A Stoke-on-Trent primary is recognised for work to highlight the dangers of illegal money lenders.
articles.body:
The story of an 83-year-old grandmother who became the oldest loan shark to be prosecuted in the UK stopped Caroline Lewis in her tracks.

The assistant principal was attending a safeguarding conference when she heard how the pensioner had been illegally lending money to parents on a school playground.

"It made me think, wow, you don't actually know who a loan shark is," said Lewis, who realised her Stoke-on-Trent school community needed to be more aware of the dangers of illegal money lending.

As a result, Star Academy, Sandyford, has become the first school in the country to be accredited by the England Illegal Money Lending Team (IMLT) for educating children and families about the risks of loan sharks.

Its pupils are also the first to be presented with copies of a children's book aimed at highlighting how illegal money lenders operate.

Parents and carers have also been given information about alternative legal lending routes, such as credit unions.

Lewis said she had not considered it a safeguarding issue before the conference, but following a number of workshops run by Stop Loan Sharks, she is now confident her pupils are very savvy.

"We had our Ofsted recently and they told the inspector about loan sharks and why they were dangerous.

Loan shark, 83, ordered to repay thousands

'Debt was a circle I could not get out of'

An estimated 1.7 million people in England owe money to an illegal lender, according to the England Illegal Money Lending Team (IMLT).

In the case Lewis heard about, Tabitha Richardson was ordered in 2024 to pay more than £173,000 after the 83-year-old was found to have been illegally lending money for 20 years.

Catherine Wohlers, the organisation's operations manager, said loan sharks are not confined to dark alleyways and back streets, and have even been known to operate around school gates.

"We've seen mums on the playground lending money to other mums," she said.

"We've also seen cases where children have almost been weaponised."

In some, the children of loan sharks have threatened borrowers' children, telling them: "Your mum owes my dad money".

Schools can also play a vital role in spotting the warning signs, Wohlers added.

One child's poor behaviour every Thursday was eventually linked to the day a loan shark came to collect repayments.

The family would routinely hide behind the sofa with the lights off.

Trigger points during the year include August and September when parents are buying school uniform, as well as the run-up to Christmas.

It can take some people years to report that they have fallen victim and there is no such thing as a "typical" loan shark, explained Wohlers.

A fifth of suspects arrested last year were female.

"We've seen people who were in no way physically intimidating, but they've been very good at psychological manipulation," she added.

"I've personally worked with people who've borrowed less than £1000 and paid back £26,000, £28,000, £30,000," Wohlers said.

"It's just a hook, basically, that loan, and they just use it to extort money."

The children's book was the idea of the National Literacy Trust and has been funded using money seized from convicted loan sharks.

Called Doubling Doubloons, it tells the tale of a cat and frog who order more ice cream than they can afford and a shark spots the opportunity to lend them money.

It is targeted at key stage two pupils and the hope is that the message it contains also makes its way to their parents.

Doubling Doubloons is being provided to schools across Stoke-on-Trent for free by the National Literacy Trust, but the aim is to make the book available more widely, said Wohlers.

The IMLT say these are the signs a loan shark may be trying to target you:

Someone lending you money who appears to to be a friend at first, but now you are not so sure

They have added extra charges or huge amounts of interest to your loan

IMLT stress that illegal money lenders are the people committing a crime, not those who borrow from them. The 24-hour helpline is 0300 555 2222.
