articles.title: Golan Heights 2.0? Why Israel's grip on southern Lebanon is raising fears
articles.summary: Israel moved into southern Lebanon to create a security buffer between its northern border and Hezbollah.
articles.body: Israel moved into southern Lebanon to create a security buffer between its northern border and Hezbollah. It aims to keep the militant group and its weapons away from Israeli communities.But what was projected as a military measure to prevent cross-border attacks is increasingly raising fears of a prolonged occupation.With Israeli forces establishing fortified positions and preparing for an extended presence, questions are mounting over whether the security zone could become permanent, much like the Golan Heights, which Israel captured from Syria in 1967 and has controlled for nearly six decades.The concerns have gained fresh momentum after an Israeli military spokesperson visited a school in Debl, a Christian-majority village inside the Israeli-controlled zone in southern Lebanon.Lt Col Ella Waweya, also known as Captain Ella, shared footage of the visit on social media. The video showed her interacting with students inside the school, which lies within the Israeli-controlled security zone.Waweya reportedly praised the beauty of southern Lebanon's villages while blaming Hezbollah for the destruction and suffering in the region.Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam strongly condemned the visit, accusing the Israeli military of exploiting schoolchildren for propaganda and attempting to legitimise its presence in southern Lebanon."The use of students in a military and propaganda display constitutes a violation of the sanctity of schools and children's rights," Salam said in a statement carried by Lebanon's National News Agency."An occupying power has no right to exploit our children to embellish the image of its occupation or impose its dominance over our people in the south," he added.The Debl municipality clarified that Waweya's visit had taken place around a month earlier, without prior coordination with the school's administration.Israeli forces currently occupy approximately 600 square kilometres of Lebanese territory, accounting for nearly 6 per cent of the country, according to a November 18 report by Defense News citing the UN peacekeeping force UNIFIL.The Israeli-controlled zone extends up to around 10 km inside Lebanon in some areas and includes military positions and fortified bases. UNIFIL has also reported continued Israeli construction of military positions and roads, demolitions and military operations inside Lebanese territory.Fears of another Golan HeightsThe Golan Heights offers a telling precedent for what could lie ahead for southern Lebanon.What began as an Israeli military capture of Syrian territory during the 1967 Six-Day War gradually turned into a decades-long occupation, with Israel extending its laws and administration to the territory in 1981.Nearly six decades later, Israel continues to control the strategic plateau despite international opposition. Now, as Israeli forces establish fortified positions and prepare for an extended presence in southern Lebanon, fears are growing that the declared security zone could follow a similar trajectory.Experts have warned that the distinction between a temporary security buffer and a prolonged occupation could become increasingly blurred.Gustav Meibauer, an assistant professor of international relations at Radboud University, told DW that the name given to such a zone matters less than what is happening on the ground."What matters is not what something is called, but what is being done", he said.Meibauer warned that if the Israeli military presence becomes a de facto permanent arrangement, with territory rendered uninhabitable and remaining under Israeli control, it could amount to an occupation under international law.HA Hellyer, a senior fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), also raised concerns that Israel could be using the current situation to establish new territorial realities in southern Lebanon."They're using this particular period to draw some new lines in the sand, to create these sort of security zones," Hellyer told DW.He pointed to the Golan Heights as an example of how Israeli security zones and territorial control could develop into long-term arrangements.The question of how long Israel intends to remain is also becoming a diplomatic flashpoint.Israeli Defence minister Israel Katz has said that Israeli forces will not withdraw until Hezbollah is disarmed and has ordered preparations for an extended military presence.Washington has pushed back, with a US state department official saying that a permanent Israeli military presence in southern Lebanon would not be consistent with the commitments made under the agreement between the two countries.For now, Israel has not announced any plan to annex southern Lebanon, and its stated objective remains the removal of Hezbollah's threat along its northern border.However, its expanding military footprint, preparations for a prolonged presence and the destruction of border villages have raised questions about whether the security zone could outlast the current conflict.With the Golan Heights serving as a historical precedent, the central concern for Lebanon is whether a buffer zone created in the name of security could eventually become a decades-long Israeli occupation.You use AI every day. articles.title: Only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi? SC mulls 5-year plan to keep commercial vehicles out
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday indicated that it may consider allowing only vehicles meeting Bharat Stage-VI (BS-VI) emission standards to operate
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday indicated that it may consider allowing only vehicles meeting Bharat Stage-VI (BS-VI) emission standards to operate in Delhi as part of efforts to tackle worsening air pollution. The bench, headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, also proposed a five-year plan to eventually keep commercial vehicles out of the national capital by shifting the unloading of goods to warehouses at Delhi's borders and using cleaner vehicles for deliveries within the city.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the observations while hearing a matter concerning air pollution in Delhi-NCR.“We are clear we will allow only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi, if not NCR,” news agency ANI quoted the bench as saying.SC proposes warehouses at Delhi borders The court suggested setting up warehouses at Delhi's borders where commercial vehicles could unload goods. These could then be transported into the city using smaller battery-operated or other non-polluting vehicles.The arrangement would ensure that essential commodities, including vegetables, fruits and other daily-use items, continue to reach residents even if commercial vehicles are barred from entering Delhi.“Why not how to ensure that commercial vehicles don't enter Delhi at all? But it does not mean that Delhi people don't require things. They have lot of necessities. They require vegetables, they require fruits, they need other day-to-day items, daily items. So everything will have to be available. So what can be the alternative?,” asked the bench.“Can there be something that at the border some warehousing so that you have some other battery-operated vehicles or non-polluting vehicles to bring them inside the city?” the CJI said.The bench clarified that the proposal may not be practical immediately but could be developed over the next five years as a long-term measure to reduce vehicular emissions.The Supreme Court is hearing suo motu proceedings on air pollution in Delhi-NCR. The case covers several sources of pollution, including firecrackers, crop residue burning and solid waste management.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO
articles.summary: Jensen Huang will return as Nvidia’s president and CEO, the company’s board announced Monday in a stunning reversal for an executive who resigned two weeks ago following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy.
articles.body: Jensen Huang will return as Nvidia’s president and CEO, the company’s board announced Monday in a stunning reversal for an executive who resigned two weeks ago following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy. The move is effective immediately, the company said in a statement. The surprise announcement sent shares of Nvidia — one of the world’s most valuable companies — surging by 30%, which in turn put the S&P 500 to open higher by almost 4%. “The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA.” The Nvidia board’s decision came after President Donald Trump on Sunday night wrote on social media, “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.” Nvidia said its decision to reinstate Huang came after “input from senior levels of the United States government.” It added that, “based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” In his own statement, Huang said he was “honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution.” Huang has served effectively as the unofficial ambassador for the artificial intelligence boom, the companies backing it and the trillions of dollars being spent in the sector. “I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support,” Huang added. The reversal was a dramatic turn, after Nvidia’s newly installed chairman Harvey Jones on Nov. 17 said: “Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as President, CEO and Board member. The Nvidia Board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” Nvidia’s inerim CEO Collette Kress also said that the company would not be reinstalling Huang in an interview the same day. Huang’s removal from Nvidia came after The New York Times reported that Huang had a close relationship with a woman who U.S. intelligence agencies believed was a Chinese spy. The Financial Times followed that report, saying that Huang had an affair with the woman. In a memo to Nvidia’s workforce on Nov. 8, Huang said, “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” The New York Times also reported Huang had an extramarital relationship with a senior leader at Nvidia who reported directly to him. After Huang’s removal, the board of the company initiated a search for a new leader, reportedly seeking out Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas. However, Haas earlier Monday announced that he was remaining at Arm, with a contract extension through 2033. Nvidia also set up a new “national security and export control oversight” panel in light of the revelations about Huang. Minutes after Huang’s return was announced, Trump posted a statement about it on social media. “The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security,” he wrote. Attorney General Todd Blanche “has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” Trump said the company’s internal probe related to export controls, announced after Huang’s initial admission of an affair, should continue. The return of Huang raises many questions for Nvidia, including the status of its dealings with overseas companies purchasing its high-powered chips, and Huang’s relationships with his subordinates at the company. Despite Trump’s statement that the U.S. government believes that Huang poses no national security risk, the company could still face legal exposure on other fronts. The Wall Street Journal and Reuters both reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is probing the company. The Journal said the probe was focused on the firm’s accounting practices. The SEC declined to comment to NBC News on Friday. Nvidia did not return a request for comment on the reports. Huang had received an outpouring of support from prominent Silicon Valley tech leaders and investors, many of whom clamored for his return. Brad Gerstner, CEO of Altimeter Capital Management, which has a significant stake in Nvidia, wrote in a letter last week co-authored with Atreides Management managing partner Gavin Baker that Nvidia’s board should keep all options on the table, including potentially asking Huang to return.

articles.title: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'
articles.summary: 21-year-old Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty to the Rockstar Games hack and others he carried out when he was a teenager.
articles.body:
A cyber criminal who hacked the maker of Grand Theft Auto has been released on licence after serving the majority of a seven-year sentence.

Multiple offender Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford, was released from custody with the judge warning him: "Don't let this happen again."

The now 21-year-old hacked several companies and individuals, including GTA 6-maker Rockstar Games, whom he tried to extort after stealing clips of the unfinished game in 2022.

Kurtaj had pleaded guilty last Monday at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar hack and a handful of others which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old with the hacking gang Lapsus$.

Kurtaj was originally sentenced to an indefinite stay in a secure hospital due to the severity of his autism.

But, in an unusual move, he was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial and released to a normal prison in January.

Now, he has been sentenced and released on the same day.

He has been given a Serious Crime Prevention Order which will last five years. It restricts his activity online including barring him from using Telegram and Discord.

City of London Police said the case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online".

He hacked Rockstar games, Revolut and Uber while on bail and under police protection in a Travelodge in Bicester.

He was there for protection from rival hackers who had threatened to attack him for his stolen stashes of Bitcoin.

With his computer confiscated, Kurtaj hacked Rockstar using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into his hotel room television along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

He stole internal company data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished GTA 6, which had been shrouded in secrecy until its release last week.

He then broke into the company's internal Slack messaging system to declare: "If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code."

The company refused to co-operate so he posted the clips and source code on a forum under the username TeaPotUberHacker.

Rockstar Games said it cost the firm $5m (£3.8m) to recover from the hack, plus thousands of hours of staff time.

The company also said the breach revealed for the first time that one of the playable characters in the game was a woman - a secret it was guarding closely for marketing purposes.

When he was sentenced he stood and smiled.

He had short hair and an unkempt beard and wore a suit and buttoned-up white shirt without a tie.

The hacker blinked frequently during the hearing.

The Judge Mr Justice Turner told him "you are a very talented young man," and warned him: "Don't let this happen again."

Kurtaj's defence team said he found the online world a more comfortable way of interacting with other people.

"The restricted and repetitive patterns of behaviour and interests that are a core feature of ASD [autism spectrum disorder] led him to become preoccupied with the online world where he felt better able to function and exist," they said.

They said he was exposed to people who showed him how to cheat at games and then to "people who were involved in hacking".

During the pandemic, he was "very isolated" and his "connection to Lapsus$ provided him with a sense of community and self-worth that had been absent in his life previously," they added.

Kurtaj and the gang's other hacks on BT/EE, Revolut and Uber used social engineering techniques - tricking people into clicking malicious links or giving up sensitive information - to gain access to internal systems.

Previously, the court heard that during his hack on Uber he posted a picture of a penis as part of his attempts to force the company to pay a ransom.

His hacks on the companies are estimated to have caused around £10m of damage.

Using the data stolen from the firms, he and other members of the gang targeted cryptocurrency investors.

The prosecution argued that the gang stole at least $300,000 (£230,000) from individual victims.

Kurtaj also pleaded guilty to physical assaults on workers while in custody, including multiple biting incidents.

In prison, he was caught with a mobile phone after sending a taunting text message to police and posting updates on Snapchat.

articles.title: Karimnagar govt medical college bars protests as students demand permanent college building, hostels
articles.summary: Karimnagar Govt Medical College bans unauthorised protests as students demand permanent campus and hostels, citing poor infrastructure and no clear timeline.
articles.body: Hyderabad: A day after BRS working president KT Rama Rao interacted with protesting students, Govt Medical College, Karimnagar, issued a notice on Monday prohibiting unauthorised gatherings, agitations and demonstrations on its campus and hospital premises.However, students continued their protest for the third consecutive day, demanding the immediate handover of their permanent college building and hostels.The circular, issued by the college principal, directed students to raise grievances through the appropriate institutional channels and refrain from participating in protests without prior permission from competent authorities. It also warned that violations could invite disciplinary action.The notice came a day after KTR, who was in Karimnagar on Nov 22, stopped to interact with protesting students and called health minister Damodar Raja Narasimha, assuring them that he would take up their concerns with the govt.Around 300 of the college’s 400 students are participating in the protest, while the fresh batch is yet to join. Students said they were waiting for nearly three years for a permanent college building and hostel facilities, despite officials repeatedly claiming that construction work was 95% complete. They alleged that successive batches had been given assurances that the college and hostel buildings would be handed over within a few months, but the deadlines kept changing without any concrete outcome.“Lack of basic infrastructure was affecting both academics and clinical training. The college has only three washrooms, which are inadequate for the strength of the institution. Moreover, poor transport arrangements add to the woes, with only two buses available for hostel commutes, one of which is frequently under repair,” said A Shashank, a final-year MBBS student.He added that the absence of hostels and adequate classrooms has forced students to depend on temporary arrangements. “First-year students have reportedly been attending online classes due to the lack of proper lecture halls,” said Shashank.The principal’s notice has also drawn criticism from former medical bodies, including FAIMA president Dr D Srinath, who questioned why students raising concerns over basic facilities were being warned against protests instead of being given a clear timeline for resolving their problems.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: Don Toliver postpones London O2 arena show after Manchester evacuation
articles.summary: His Manchester show on Sunday was evacuated after an "unknown substance" was released into the crowd.
articles.body:
US rapper Don Toliver has postponed his concert at the O2 arena in London on Monday after his show in Manchester on Sunday was evacuated following an "unknown substance" being released into the crowd.

"I'm very sad to sit here and say I have to reschedule The O2 London show to December 15th due to unfortunate incident last night Manchester," he wrote on Instagram.

"I just wanna make sure everyone is safe and the next show goes on properly. My heart and prayers are with with everyone that was injured last night."

Toliver is also scheduled to perform at Wembley Arena on Tuesday. No update has been given about that show.

Police investigate unknown substance that caused Manchester's Co-op Live evacuation

The Manchester incident happened towards the end of Toliver's show at the Co-op Live arena at about 22:00 GMT on Sunday, with fans describing a "horrible smell" and people "screaming" and "coughing up blood".

One person was taken to hospital while more than 80 people were assessed for "eye and respiratory symptoms", the North West Ambulance Service said.

Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said a major incident was declared after reports of people suffering from the effects of an unknown substance, which police initially believed to be tear gas.

The force said 12,000 people had been evacuated and one fan told of "distressing scenes" with people "choking" and coughing as they left the venue.

Some fans have complained about security and a lack of searches going in to the concert.

articles.title: Telangana releases ₹5.6 crore to 214 surrendered Maoists; DGP appeals to  Maoist Leader Ganapathi and two others to give up arms
articles.summary: Telangana disburses ₹5.6 crore to 214 surrendered Maoists; DGP CV Anand urges leader Ganapathi and others to surrender, citing rehab support and safety measures.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Director general of police CV Anand on Monday appealed to former CPI (Maoist) general secretary Muppala Laxman Rao alias Ganapathi and two other remaining Maoist leaders from Telangana to surrender.“We do not know where they are. There is no information on whether they are still alive. However, we appeal to them to surrender. The police assure them that we will take care of them,” Anand said while distributing cheques to 214 former Maoist cadres who had surrendered.The state disbursed a total of Rs 5.59 crore to the 214 cadres. At the time of their surrender, they were given an interim relief of Rs 25,000 each, with the remaining rehabilitation assistance distributed on Monday. The delay in releasing the funds was due to the absence of Aadhaar cards. The police coordinated with officials in Chhattisgarh to facilitate the issuance of Aadhaar cards.Of the 214 surrendered cadres, 59 are from Telangana, while the remaining are from Chhattisgarh. Of the 59 surrendered cadres, 10 have been allotted house sites, while efforts are underway to secure similar benefits for the others.With the latest disbursement of Rs 5.59 crore, Telangana has distributed Rs 17 crore to 659 surrendered Maoist cadres since the beginning of Operation Kagar in 2024. Meanwhile, 96 eligible cadres will receive their cash rewards once their Aadhaar cards and bank accounts are arranged.The DGP also said that the general public would not be allowed access to Karregutta Hills, once a Maoist stronghold, as the area remains littered with explosive mines. “It will take some time before we allow public access. Greyhounds personnel are working to identify and clear the explosive dumps, and the operation is still underway,” he said.Police officials said they were regularly interacting with surrendered cadres to facilitate their rehabilitation through employment opportunities and skill development programmes.They added that former Maoist leaders who had expressed a desire to engage in political activities were now being allowed to participate in meetings.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: Sentenced to life for sister's murder, Thane convict jumps to death from  court's 5th floor
articles.summary: THANE: In a shocking turn of events at a court in Thane district on Monday, a 28-year-old convict jumped to his death from the building's fifth floor,
articles.body: THANE: In a shocking turn of events at a court in Thane district on Monday, a 28-year-old convict jumped to his death from the building's fifth floor, minutes after being sentenced to life imprisonment for murdering his sister in 2019 and to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment for attempting to kill his wife.The incident occurred in the afternoon when court officials and police personnel were completing post-conviction formalities. The convict, identified as Nagesh Babu Lad, darted out of the courtroom and jumped from the fifth floor.Earlier, the additional sessions judge of the Belapur court had convicted Lad under various sections of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced him to life imprisonment for murdering his sister and 10 years of rigorous imprisonment for attempting to kill his wife in a 2019 case.According to the prosecution, Lad suspected that his wife was having an extra-marital affair with his brother-in-law. In the early hours of July 17, 2019, he assaulted her with a knife on the terrace of her paternal house in Navi Mumbai before fleeing.He then went to his sister's residence. She had tried to pacify him and help her sister-in-law, but he stabbed her multiple times in the chest with a knife, leading to her death due to haemorrhage and shock.Holding that the prosecution had established the charge of attempt to murder his wife, the court observed, "The cumulative effect of all these circumstances leads to draw the inference that the accused assaulted witness Jyotsna (Lad's wife) with a dangerous weapon."The injury inflicted was with intention and knowledge to commit murder of victim Jyotsna. The hurt caused was grievous in nature. The injury was life-threatening. Therefore, though the victim was survived, it was an attempt to commit murder by the accused," the court said.On the murder of Lad's sister Sunita, the court found a complete chain of circumstances pointing to his guilt, even though some witnesses had turned hostile. These included the recovery of the knife, identification of the knife seller at the accused's instance, recovery of blood-stained clothes and WhatsApp messages."From her testimony inference can be drawn that due to suspicion that his wife was having illicit relation with his brother-in-law, the accused has made stab injury to her and told her that he was going to kill Jarmanjit Singh (his brother-in-law)," the court stated in its order.The court noted that Lad had planned to murder his wife, but when his sister tried to pacify him, he angrily killed her."The case is not a rarest of rare one. The accused is a young offender. His mental condition at the time of committing the offence was suspicion in his mind that his wife had an illicit relationship."His criminal antecedents have not come on record. Therefore, life imprisonment for the offence under IPC section 302 and rigorous imprisonment of ten years for the offence punishable under section 307 would suffice the purpose," the judge added.(With PTI inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Thane | Silver Rate in Thane | Bank Holidays in Thane | Public Holidays in Thane | Petrol Price in Thane | Diesel Price in Thane | CNG Price in Thane | LPG Price in ThaneStay updated with the latest Thane news. articles.title: Iran vows to end U.S. naval blockade by "all available means"
articles.summary: Iran vows to force the U.S. to lift its blockade as Trump acknowledges the regime's increasing attacks, but says they've "done no damage."
articles.body:
Iran said Monday it would use "all available means" to counter the U.S. naval blockade of the country's ports, which a foreign ministry official described as "an act of military aggression" against the country.President Trump said in a social media post on Sunday that Iran had "launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time" during the nearly-nine-month war , but that the increasing attacks had "done no damage." A media outlet linked to Iran's Houthi allies said Monday that a Saudi attack on Yemen's port city of Hodeida killed four people and wounded 18, as fighting between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis continues to intensify.

Netanyahu foe trying to form new Israeli government says no "immediate threat" requiring action against Iran

Gadi Eisenkot, the Israeli politician trying to form a new government to oust current Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the wake of national elections, has said he sees no "immediate threat" from Iran requiring military action.

Speaking at a meeting of his party, Yashar, Monday, he said: "I see no direct and immediate threat from Iran today that would require Israel to act before a new government is formed."

He added that "the gravest threat Iran poses" comes from its stockpile on enriched uranium: "That is where we need to focus."

Netanyahu has appeared keen to go on the offensive against Iran again. Sources familiar with the matter told CBS News last week that Israel and the U.S. were considering a new assault on the country .

Eisenkot recently said Netanyahu should not make any big national security decisions in the transition period following Israel's election, in which Netanyahu's bloc lost its majority, and that the now-caretaker prime minister should avoid "dangerous steps that can wait for the swearing in of a new government."

Iran seeks $290 billion in damages against the U.S.

Iran is due $290 billion from the United States to cover damages inflicted both during, and long before the war launched jointly by the U.S. and Israel almost nine months ago, Iran's judiciary authorities say.

Iranian courts have demanded the U.S. pay the sum, a judiciary official said Monday.

"We have secured court rulings in domestic courts awarding $290 billion in damages against the Americans," said Hassan Abdolianpour, head of the judiciary's center for lawyers, according to state television.

He also said several lawsuits had been filed against Persian Gulf Arab nations for "allowing their territory to be used by America to launch attacks against Iran."

According to state TV, the damages cover U.S. actions going back decades.

On Monday, state broadcaster IRIB said several U.S.-linked commercial ships had been seized and that part of the compensation owed to Iran would be settled through the seizures, without giving further details.

Lebanon denounces Israeli military official's visit to school in south

Lebanese officials have denounced a visit by an Israeli military spokesperson to a school in an Israeli-occupied area of southern Lebanon.

As Lebanon marked its independence day on Sunday, the Israeli military's Arabic-language spokesperson Ella Waweya shared a video on social media showing her outside a school in Debl, a Christian village, and then standing in front of a classroom full of children.

The village is located inside a wide swath of southern Lebanon that Israel has occupied and declared a "security zone" after the latest war erupted with Hezbollah in March. The zone covers a strip of southern Lebanon along the border and stretches about six miles into Lebanese territory.

Debl is among a number of Christian-majority villages near the border where many residents have refused to leave despite Israeli military orders to evacuate. Cut off from the rest of Lebanon, they are largely dependent on humanitarian aid.

"During my last visit to south Lebanon, I was amazed by the beauty of the land and the villages which have paid a heavy price due to their exploitation ... by a terrorist organization," Waweya said, referring to the Iran-backed Hezbollah militant group.

Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam denounced Israel for "dragging students into a military and propaganda display."

"An occupying power has no right to exploit our children to embellish the image of its occupation or impose its dominance over our people in the south," he added.

Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war in March with rocket fire at Israel, which responded with massive airstrikes and a ground invasion. Lebanon says Israeli attacks since then have killed more than 4,300 people.

Iran says will use "all available means" to counter U.S. blockade

Iran said Monday it would use all means at its disposal to counter a U.S. naval blockade imposed in retaliation for its own push to block the Strait of Hormuz.

"We will certainly not tolerate these actions and will use all available means to counter U.S. aggression," foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said in his weekly press briefing.

Soon after the war broke out, the Strait of Hormuz became the focus of the conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the waterway, vital to global energy supplies.

In response, the U.S. imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. It later announced a raft of economic sanctions, and launched a task force to disrupt land routes into Iran.

"You should bear in mind that what the Americans have described as economic sanctions, an economic blockade and a naval blockade undoubtedly constitutes an act of military aggression against Iran," said Baqaei. "Under these circumstances, Iran is entitled, pursuant to Article 51 of the U.N. Charter, to use any means at its disposal to defend itself."

Iran has said Hormuz could be open within two days but only if Washington agreed to its list of demands , which include the lifting of the blockade.

Houthi media say 4 dead in Saudi attack on key port city

Houthi media said Monday that a Saudi attack killed four people and wounded 18 in Yemen's key port city of Hodeida.

The Iran-backed fighters, who control large swathes of Yemen including Hodeida, are battling a Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen's internationally recognized government.

The strike targeted a building belonging to Yemen's Public Telecommunications Corporation, the Houthis' Almasirah television channel wrote on X.

Riyadh didn't immediately comment on the report.

It came a day after the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched toward the kingdom's western Red Sea coast.

That region is home to major oil installations that Houthi fighters have attacked in recent weeks, along with strikes on airports and military sites.

Yemen, which has been embroiled in more than a decade of civil war, was sucked into the U.S.-Iran conflict in July when a truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government unraveled.

Since then, hostilities have left more than 1,600 people dead and more than 300,000 displaced in the country, the poorest on the Arabian Peninsula, according to the latest U.N. data.

Houthis say Saudi strike on Yemen capital wounds 6

Houthi rebels in Yemen reported an airstrike early Sunday in the capital, Sanaa.

A spokesperson for the Houthi-run Health Ministry, Anees al-Asbahi, said the strike hit a fuel station operated by the state-run oil company and wounded six workers.

The strike also damaged the company's building, al-Asbahi said.

The Red Sea port city of Mokha also came under fire on Sunday, Houthi-run television reported, as did the Haifan district in the southwestern province of Taiza.

The Houthis blamed Saudi Arabia for the airstrikes but didn't report any casualties from them.

Trump says Iran launched more drones and missiles in past week "than at any time for over a year"

President Trump on Sunday acknowledged that Iran "has launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time for over a year," but he added: "Don't worry, they've all been knocked down, and done no damage."

In a post on Truth Social, the president linked the midterm elections — in which Democrats won majorities in both chambers of Congress — to the escalation in the war with Iran.

"As everyone remembers, I predicted two things concerning the November 3rd Midterm Elections. One, that if the Democrats win, the Stock Markets would go down, substantially, which they have, and two, that the Islamic Republic of Iran, which has killed 81,000 protestors as of today, will grow more aggressive in their attacks, which has also occurred," Mr. Trump said.

Higher fuel prices triggered by the war caused economic concerns for Americans, and top Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance, have partly attributed GOP election defeats to the war with Iran.

Mr. Trump on Sunday said voters "didn't understand" what their votes meant and called the election "very 'strange.'"

"Iranian leaders consider the Democrats weak, ineffective, and Country destroying, but I won't let that happen! Both the Dems and Iran fought like hell to keep the Oil price up as long as possible and, since the Election, the Oil price has dropped by a record level," he said. "Too bad the Voters didn't understand this before they pulled the trigger, but the whole Election was very 'strange.'"

Athlete swims Strait of Hormuz to raise awareness of Iran war's toll on wildlife

British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh has swum in the North Pole and Antarctica to draw attention to environmental causes. But battling freezing waters and extreme conditions hasn't prepared him for his latest challenge: swimming the Strait of Hormuz while tankers are attacked and blown up nearby.

Pugh, who is a United Nations Patron of the Oceans, spent three days this week swimming parts of the dangerous waterway to highlight how the war with Iran threatens the area's habitat and wildlife.

Wearing only swimming trunks, goggles and a cap bearing the U.N. logo, the athlete started from the Musandam Peninsula, on the southern tip of the strait, and ended by rounding the Cape of Hormuz, completing about 9.3 miles in total. Pugh is believed to be the first person to undertake a long-distance swim there since the war started.

The swimmer said that minutes after he entered the water on Monday, he heard two loud explosions that rocked the sea.

Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Saturday that a Qatari delegation visited Tehran the previous evening and "held two hours of talks," without providing details.

Negotiations between the U.S. and Iran to end the war have stalled in recent months.

Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said, however, that ongoing talks in the region must be "given a chance" and that the ongoing U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz "must be lifted rationally."

"Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless," he said, quoted by state television.

"At the same time, we have always affirmed our readiness for dialogue, just as we are ready to defend ourselves."

Iran's conditions have included ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the U.S. counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

Trump says he wants to make "permanent" deal with Iranian regime

President Trump said Saturday that he wants to make a "permanent" deal with Iran that will prevent the country from gaining a nuclear weapon in the future.

"What I'm doing is I'm going to make it so that if we have an incompetent president in four years or 15 years or 20 years, I'm going to make a deal that is going to be permanent," Mr. Trump told Fox News in a phone interview on Saturday. "I'm not going to let somebody allow them to have a nuclear weapon."

Mr. Trump said he's never "cared too much about the regime" leading Iran, and that he has "taken out two regimes already," though he declined to specify further. Former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed in the initial strikes on Iran that began the war in February 2026. His son Mojtaba Khamenei has held the title ever since.

Mr. Trump said Iranian officials have been "very, very difficult" to make a deal with.

"I mean, we make a deal and then they break the deal the next day," Mr. Trump said.
